questions.stem: A client taking warfarin has an INR of 5.2 with no signs of bleeding. Which action should the nurse anticipate?

options.label: A
options.text: Continue warfarin at the same dose
options.rationale: An INR above the therapeutic range of 2 to 3 carries a high bleeding risk, so continuing the same dose is unsafe.

options.label: B
options.text: Hold the warfarin and prepare to give vitamin K if prescribed
options.rationale: Warfarin is held for a supratherapeutic INR, and vitamin K is the antidote the provider may prescribe to bring the INR down.

options.label: C
options.rationale: Protamine sulfate reverses heparin, not warfarin, and would not correct a high INR.

questions.teachingPoint: Therapeutic INR on warfarin is 2 to 3; vitamin K reverses warfarin, protamine reverses heparin.

questions.stem: A client is two days post-operative after a total hip replacement. The nurse notes that the right calf is swollen, warm and tender. What should the nurse do?

options.label: A
options.text: Massage the calf to relieve the discomfort
options.rationale: Massaging a possible deep vein thrombosis can dislodge the clot and cause a pulmonary embolism.

options.label: B
options.text: Keep the client in bed, notify the provider and anticipate a venous duplex ultrasound
options.rationale: A swollen, warm, tender calf after hip surgery suggests deep vein thrombosis; limiting movement and prompt evaluation prevent embolization.

options.label: C
options.text: Encourage the client to ambulate to improve circulation
options.rationale: Ambulation is prevention, not treatment; with a suspected clot, walking may cause it to break loose.

questions.subtopic: Potential for Complications from Surgical Procedures and Health Alterations
questions.teachingPoint: Post-operative unilateral calf swelling, warmth and tenderness is deep vein thrombosis until proven otherwise: do not massage, notify the provider.

questions.stem: The nurse is preparing a client for a cardiac catheterization. Which finding should the nurse report to the provider before the procedure?

options.label: A
options.text: The client reports an allergy to shellfish and iodine
options.rationale: Iodinated contrast is used during catheterization; a reported iodine or contrast allergy needs premedication or an alternative plan.

options.label: B
options.text: The client's blood pressure is 128 over 78
options.rationale: This blood pressure is within normal limits and does not affect the procedure.

options.label: C
options.text: The client has had nothing to eat for eight hours
options.rationale: Fasting before the procedure is expected and required, not a concern to report.

questions.teachingPoint: Before contrast studies, screen for contrast or iodine allergy, kidney function and metformin use, and confirm fasting status.
